=== DOCS-TRUTH RE-PINNED (verified against trino.io/docs/467 mental model) ===
• MATCH_RECOGNIZE — Trino 467 funnel/sequential-pattern shape: `<table_or_subquery> MATCH_RECOGNIZE ( PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ... MEASURES <expr> AS <alias>, ... ONE ROW PER MATCH | ALL ROWS PER MATCH AFTER MATCH SKIP TO NEXT ROW | TO LAST <label> | PAST LAST ROW | TO FIRST <label> PATTERN (label1 label2+ label3*) DEFINE label1 AS <pred>, label2 AS <pred>, ... )`. Quantifiers: `?` 0-or-1, `+` 1-or-more, `*` 0-or-more, `{n}` exact, `{n,m}` range. Navigation functions in MEASURES/DEFINE: `FIRST(expr [, occurrence])`, `LAST(expr [, occurrence])`, `PREV(expr [, n])`, `NEXT(expr [, n])`. Within-N-time-window via `event_time <= FIRST(event_time) + INTERVAL '7' DAY` predicate inside DEFINE. Supported in Trino, Snowflake, Oracle; NOT in Postgres/MySQL/BigQuery/DuckDB.
• RANGE-INTERVAL window — Trino 467 calendar-aware rolling window: `<agg>(x) OVER (ORDER BY <date_or_ts_or_numeric_col> RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '<n>' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)` for trailing N-day calendar rolling. RANGE is VALUE-based — frame includes all rows whose ORDER BY value falls within the interval, NOT a count of physical rows. Counts CALENDAR DAYS, NOT physical rows — distinct from `ROWS BETWEEN N PRECEDING` (positional). Gap-day correct: missing days simply contribute zero rows. **Required pre-aggregate-to-one-row-per-day-first caveat** when source has multiple rows per day (e.g., per-order/per-event table): RANGE INTERVAL over a non-unique ORDER BY key on the raw table will pull MORE rows than intended within the interval; the correct shape is a daily CTE first (`SUM(metric) GROUP BY order_date`), then `<agg>(daily_metric) OVER (ORDER BY order_date RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '6' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)`. Without the pre-aggregate, per-event averaging is also broken (averaging individual order amounts, not daily totals). Both bugs (ROWS-vs-RANGE grain + per-event-vs-per-day amount) fixed by the SAME pre-aggregate edit. ORDER BY column must be numeric/DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ; offset must be matching INTERVAL type. Verified at trino.io/docs/current/functions/window.html (since Trino 346, March 2021).
• GROUPING SETS + GROUPING() bitmask — Trino 467 form: `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((col1, col2), (col1), ())` emits ONE group per listed tuple; `GROUP BY ROLLUP(a, b)` = `GROUPING SETS ((a,b), (a), ())` (N+1 emissions, trailing-drop only); `GROUP BY CUBE(a, b)` = `GROUPING SETS ((a,b), (a), (b), ())` (2^N emissions, full power set). `GROUPING(c1, c2, ..., cN)` returns an integer bitmask: **LEFTMOST arg is the HIGH (most-significant) bit; bit is SET (=1) when the column is ROLLED UP / AGGREGATED AWAY; bit is 0 when the column is PRESENT in the grouping**. For `GROUPING(a, b)`: 0 = binary 00 = both present (detail row), 1 = binary 01 = b rolled up (per-A subtotal), 2 = binary 10 = a rolled up (per-B subtotal), 3 = binary 11 = both rolled up (grand total). 2-column ROLLUP never emits value 2 (ROLLUP only drops trailing columns). `GROUPING_ID(c1, c2, ...)` is an alias for `GROUPING(c1, c2, ...)`. Use `CASE GROUPING(a, b) WHEN 0 THEN 'Detail' WHEN 1 THEN 'A Subtotal' WHEN 2 THEN 'B Subtotal' WHEN 3 THEN 'Grand Total' END` to label row types in a CUBE result.
• CROSS JOIN UNNEST multiple arrays + WITH ORDINALITY — Trino 467 form: (single array) `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(arr) AS t(elem)` explodes one row per element (DROPS rows whose array is NULL or empty); `LEFT JOIN UNNEST(arr) AS t(elem) ON TRUE` KEEPS parent rows with NULL/empty array (NULL-padded). (multiple arrays) `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(arr1, arr2) AS t(a, b)` zips element-wise by position — same-index elements paired; shorter array padded with NULL to match the longer. (with ordinality) `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(arr) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(elem, idx)` — ordinality column appended as the LAST column in the alias list (element first, ordinality LAST), 1-based array index. Combinable: `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(arr1, arr2) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(a, b, idx)` zip + 1-based position. `UNNEST(map_col)` over a MAP column yields key,value pairs: `CROSS JOIN UNNEST(my_map) AS t(k, v)`. JOIN UNNEST is FROM-clause syntax — must precede WHERE.
